items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: So I went to Edward G. Robinson in his dressing room, and I asked him for a photograph.

ctx.x: with some of these celebrities that I have worked with and know -- I knew 'em on a first-name basis. I can't come up to the children nowadays and say, "Well, I know so-and-so-and-so. I worked with him," and this-that-and-the-other. They'd say, "That old man is crazy. He just said he knows so-and-so..." Well, that's the way they think of you.

No, I never thought about getting together with them and having my picture taken, and this-that-and-the-other. The nearest I come to anything like that, I worked the Palace Theatre...oh, this is way back in the Thirties. Edward G. Robinson was on the bill and Kate Smith was on the bill, and Bessie Love -- Bessie Love was a movie star. Well, Edward G. Robinson at that time, he was just starting in pictures. He was a big man, he was a big star. So I went to Edward G. Robinson in his dressing room, and I asked him…

But I mean, I had never did anything like that! And all down through my career I never did it no more. I got Edward G. Robinson's and Bessie Love's -- Kate Smith didn't have any photographs of herself. I didn't get none of her anyway, and I worked with her twice. I didn't ask her for one the second time. But Bessie Love I got. And I got 'em,
